prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of key proposals (non-exhaustive)

Fiscal and tax
- Cut the deficit every year; achieve a surplus on the current budget and get debt falling as soon as possible; no new commitments funded by additional borrowing.
- Independent auditing of manifesto costings by the Office for Budget Responsibility.
- Cap structural welfare spending in each spending review.
- Restore the 50p top income tax rate above £150,000; introduce a 10p starting rate funded by replacing the marriage allowance.
- No rises in the basic or higher rates of Income Tax, National Insurance or VAT; no VAT extension to essentials.
- Abolish non-domiciled tax status; close avoidance loopholes; public beneficial ownership registers in Overseas Territories/Crown Dependencies; HMRC culture review.
- Use proceeds from sales of state banking stakes to reduce debt.

Economy, productivity, infrastructure, energy
- National Infrastructure Commission; support HS2 with cost control; improve northern rail; strategic roads and cycling; swift decision on airport capacity.
- Long-term science and innovation framework; university–industry “knowledge clusters.”
- Low-carbon industrial strategy: legal target to decarbonise power by 2030; empower the Green Investment Bank; Energy Security Board; robust shale regulation; support offshore oil and gas; aim for 1m additional green jobs.
- Universal affordable high‑speed broadband and improved mobile coverage; reduce digital exclusion.
- Corporate governance reforms: investor duties for long-termism, tighter takeover rules and public interest test, employee voice on remuneration.
- Support co‑ops/mutuals via a British Investment Bank; retain 30% public ownership of Royal Mail and create an employee trust.

Small business and finance
- Small Business Administration; crack down on late payment.
- Cut then freeze business rates for over 1.5m smaller properties.
- British Investment Bank and regional banks; increase banking competition; levy on payday lenders to support credit unions.

Work, pay, skills
- Raise the National Minimum Wage to over £8 by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage through procurement and first‑year tax rebates; reporting on Living Wage status.
- Ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts; close agency-worker pay loopholes; replace employment tribunal fee system.
- Guarantee an apprenticeship for every school leaver with the grades; expand high‑quality, longer apprenticeships; create Technical Degrees and Institutes of Technical Education; stronger careers advice.
- Reduce university tuition fees to £6,000; regulate unpaid internships.
- Compulsory Jobs Guarantee for long‑term unemployed, funded by a bank bonus tax; Youth Allowance tied to training.

Public services, health and care
- Recruit 8,000 GPs, 20,000 nurses and 3,000 midwives, funded by a mansion tax on £2m+ properties, a tobacco levy and anti‑avoidance measures.
- 48‑hour GP appointment guarantee; one‑week cancer tests by 2020; Cancer Treatments Fund.
- Integrate physical, mental and social care; parity for mental health; prevention focus (obesity, alcohol, activity, food standards); improve patient safety and professional regulation.
- End 15‑minute social care visits; recruit 5,000 home‑care workers; support carers.

Families, housing, markets
- Expand free childcare for working parents of 3–4‑year‑olds from 15 to 25 hours; guarantee wraparound primary school care; double paternity leave to four weeks and increase pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first call for local first‑time buyers; “use it or lose it” land powers; back small builders; garden cities; tackle empty homes.
- Private renting: three‑year tenancies as standard, ceiling on excessive rent rises, ban unfair letting fees, landlord register; reverse the Bedroom Tax; reduce homelessness.
- Energy: freeze household bills until 2017 while reforming the market (separate generation/supply, open exchange, stronger watchdog); mass home‑efficiency loans and upgrades.
- Water: national affordability scheme; stronger regulator powers.
- Transport: reform rail franchising, allow a public operator, freeze fares for one year, cap future rises; right to cheapest ticket; devolve bus powers.

Immigration, policing, justice
- 1,000 extra border staff funded by a charge on non‑visa visitors; full exit checks; tighter short‑term student visa controls; maintain non‑EU work cap.
- Two‑year wait for EU migrants to claim benefits; English requirement for public‑facing workers; ban overseas‑only recruitment; extend Gangmasters Licensing Authority; end indefinite detention for specified groups; uphold refugee obligations.
- Protect neighbourhood policing; abolish elected police commissioners; Local Policing Commitment; new Police Standards Authority; tougher action on antisocial behaviour; victims’ law; youth justice reform; ban “legal highs.”
- Violence against women and girls bill; commissioner; stable refuge/Rape Crisis funding; tighter gun licensing; DNA retention changes; wider legal aid access.

Devolution, rights, media
- English Devolution Act transferring £30bn and powers over transport, skills, housing and business support; retain growth in local business rates; local Public Accounts Committees.
- Constitutional Convention; replace the House of Lords with an elected Senate of the Nations and Regions.
- Votes at 16–17; stronger electoral registration; statutory lobbyist register; ban paid directorships/consultancies for MPs; expand Freedom of Information.
- Gender pay gap reporting for large firms; race equality strategy; uphold the Human Rights Act and engagement with the European Court of Human Rights; zero tolerance of hate crime; implement press regulation reforms and strengthen media plurality; keep Channel 4 public; ensure BBC value‑for‑money.

Foreign policy, defence, development, climate
- EU membership with reforms (single market completion, budget discipline, safeguards for non‑euro members); no transfer of powers without an in/out referendum lock; stronger role for national parliaments (“red card”).
- NATO commitment; criteria‑based approach to interventions; support a two‑state solution; Asia engagement taskforce.
- Strategic Defence and Security Review in year one; veterans’ register and protections; Military Covenant in the NHS Constitution; cyber‑security measures; maintain a continuous at‑sea nuclear deterrent while advancing multilateral disarmament.
- Lead on climate diplomacy (net‑zero global goal in second half of the century, five‑yearly strengthening cycles).
- Maintain 0.7% GNI for development; focus on the poorest and fragile states; Centre for Universal Health Coverage; tax transparency and anti‑corruption; slavery‑free, fair supply chains.

Arts, sport, environment
- Universal creative education entitlement; free national museum admission; more creative‑industry apprenticeships; fan representation in football governance; grassroots sport funding; two hours’ school sport weekly.
- Flood prevention priority; local air‑quality powers; forests in public ownership; animal‑welfare measures; strategy for food, farming and fisheries; stronger supermarket watchdog.
